simple: A micro gamepad is a small controller with only arrow buttons and a few others, like a TV remote. Some players play Roblox on a TV with just a remote, so your menus should work with up, down, left, right, select, and back. Right now remote buttons show up in scripts as normal gamepad buttons, so this page shows a trick to tell a remote apart from a full controller and how to bind actions for both.
analogy: Playing with a TV remote is like getting around a building using only the elevator buttons: up, down, open, and close. Your game has to make sure every room can be reached with just those.
keyPoints: Micro gamepads, like TV remotes, usually have a directional pad, a center button, and a back button.
`Enum.PreferredInput.MicroGamepad` exists but is not set yet, so detect remotes another way for now.
`Gamepad1` is always the player's main controller. If it supports neither `Thumbstick1` nor `Thumbstick2`, it is a micro gamepad.
If it also supports `ButtonCenter`, it is a TV remote.
For now, remote buttons arrive as legacy gamepad buttons: Center becomes `ButtonA`, Back becomes `ButtonB`, and arrows become D-pad or thumbstick input depending on context.
Do not use those legacy keycodes alone to spot a remote, because a full gamepad sends the same ones.
Bind actions with the Input Action System for new games, or keep `ContextActionService` if you already use it.
Design TV menus with a clear highlighted item, everything reachable with arrows, center to select, back to close, and big buttons.
Test with the Device Emulator set to Android TV and the Controller Emulator's TV Remote.

terms.micro gamepad: A small controller made for moving around menus, with arrows and a few buttons but no thumbsticks.
terms.D-pad: The plus-shaped arrow buttons: up, down, left, and right.
terms.legacy keycode: An older button name that Roblox currently sends instead of the remote's own button name, like `ButtonA` for the center button.
terms.Gamepad1: The slot for the player's main controller. Roblox has slots `Gamepad1` to `Gamepad8`.
terms.focus: Which button or item in a menu is currently selected and will react when you press select.
terms.ContextActionService: An older service for binding keys and buttons to named actions.
terms.Sink / Pass: In `ContextActionService`, `Sink` means your code used the input, so stop there. `Pass` lets other actions handle it too.
terms.10-foot experience: Designing for someone sitting about 10 feet (3 meters) from a TV, so text and buttons must be big.

example.title: Detect a TV remote or micro gamepad
example.code:
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")

local function isMicroGamepadPreferred()
	local gamepad = Enum.UserInputType.Gamepad1
	if not UserInputService:GetGamepadConnected(gamepad) then
		return false
	end
	-- A micro gamepad has no thumbsticks
	local hasLeftStick = UserInputService:GamepadSupports(gamepad, Enum.KeyCode.Thumbstick1)
	local hasRightStick = UserInputService:GamepadSupports(gamepad, Enum.KeyCode.Thumbstick2)
	return not hasLeftStick and not hasRightStick
end

local function isTVRemotePreferred()
	return isMicroGamepadPreferred()
		and UserInputService:GamepadSupports(Enum.UserInputType.Gamepad1, Enum.KeyCode.ButtonCenter)
end

-- The remote's center button currently arrives as ButtonA
UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(function(input, gameProcessed)
	if gameProcessed then
		return
	end
	if input.KeyCode == Enum.KeyCode.ButtonA then
		if isMicroGamepadPreferred() then
			print("Select the highlighted menu item")
		else
			print("Normal gamepad: jump or confirm")
		end
	end
end)

print("TV remote?", isTVRemotePreferred())
explain: If that controller has no left or right thumbstick, it must be a micro gamepad.
`isTVRemotePreferred` also checks for a center button, which TV remotes have.
When `ButtonA` is pressed, we check which device it came from and do the right thing: select a menu item for remotes, or jump for full gamepads.

watchOut: Assuming `ButtonA` means a full gamepad. A TV remote's center button sends `ButtonA` too.
Relying on `PreferredInput.MicroGamepad` today. It is not set yet, so use the thumbstick check.
Making menus that need a mouse or thumbstick to reach some buttons. Every item must be reachable with arrows.
Using the same input context for menu navigation and gameplay, so one button press does two things. Keep them separate.
